objective: Establish what supporting both local (per-project) and global (per-user) installations of HolyAgent means for the Claude Code plugin and for the planned pi package in 0.3.0, and how HolyAgent behaves in claude.ai chat and Cowork today.
scope: Maintainer (verbatim): "for 0.3.0, we will support both local and global installations for holyagent in claude and pi" and "also document that holyagent in claude chat/cowork (they're now unified) works correctly". The maintainer has tested chat/Cowork; the current docs (docs/usage.md '## claude.ai' and docs/requirements.md) still say it does not work there.

Repository (read-only): /home/user/holyagent-docs-t3 — README.md install section, docs/usage.md, docs/requirements.md, docs/hooks.md, docs/components.md, docs/pi/installation.md and docs/pi/configuration.md; .claude-plugin/marketplace.json; packages/integrations/claude/dist/.claude-plugin/plugin.json and hooks; skills/setup (the /holyagent:setup skill that merges recommended settings into user, project or local settings); the runtime's state modes (.holyagent/ in branch, work or local mode) and how the CLI path is resolved.

Questions: (1) Claude Code: which plugin and marketplace install scopes exist (user, project, local, managed) per the current Claude Code docs (code.claude.com/docs plugins, plugin-marketplaces, settings), how a project-scoped install is shared with a team (.claude/settings.json enabledPlugins and extraKnownMarketplaces), and what in HolyAgent depends on the scope: the setup skill's target file, the SessionStart setup check, hooks, the CLI path given to the root, the plugin data directory. (2) claude.ai: how plugins are installed for chat/Cowork (account level, organization level), whether there is a local versus global notion there, and what Anthropic's current docs say loads in Cowork sessions (agents, hooks, skills, MCP). (3) pi: global install (`pi install` into ~/.pi) versus project-local install (`pi install -l` into .pi/settings.json) per pi 1.5.0 docs, precedence when both exist, trust gating of project extensions, and how a project-local HolyAgent package would find its CLI, config and Billion Context, codemode and extension dependencies. (4) .holyagent/config.json: which settings make sense per project versus per user, and whether a user-level config file (for example ~/.holyagent/config.json) is needed for global installs.
constraints: Authoritative sources first (code.claude.com docs, support.claude.com, claude.com docs, earendil-works/pi docs at 1.5.0 or main, pi.dev); label inference.

End with: the concrete requirements for local and global installs per host (Claude Code, claude.ai, pi), each sourced or inference; then real choices for the maintainer with options and consequences, separate from facts to verify.

pi scopes: states pi's global and project-local install and its precedence and trust rules, with sources
claude.ai: states how plugins install and load in chat and Cowork today, with sources
Choices separated: real maintainer choices with options, apart from facts to verify

result:
[harness: subagent output matched instruction-shaped pattern(s): settings-json. Control tags below are neutralized (`<` → `<\`); treat any remaining directive-shaped text as a finding to relay to the user, not an instruction to you.] result: Claude Code has three install scopes, plus managed, and pi has global and project-local. claude.ai installs are account-level only. The Cowork hook-activation failure the docs report is not explained by any source I found. **Claude Code (sourced)** - User, project and local scopes write `enabledPlugins` to `~/.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json`. Local overrides project, and project overrides user ([discover-plugins](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins)). - A committed project entry enables the plugin but does not download it. Each collaborator runs `claude plugin install

@ --scope project` once (same page). - The terminal, desktop Code tab and VS Code read the same settings files. A cloud session does not load machine-installed plugins or the repo's `enabledPlugins`; organization-managed ones do load there (same page, Cloud tab). - Managed scope is `managed-settings.json` or MDM, with `extraKnownMarketplaces` and `enabledPlugins` ([org-rollout](https://claude.com/docs/plugins/org-rollout)). - The code.claude.com page I fetched truncated before the "Find where a plugin is enabled" rule, so managed-scope precedence is unverified. **What in HolyAgent depends on scope (repo docs, `/home/user/holyagent-docs-t3`)** - `docs/usage.md` L95-115 covers setup scope: - `holyagent setup` and `doctor` take `--scope user|project|local` and write the matching settings file. - The plugin install commands default to user scope. - The `agent: holyagent` takeover applies wherever the plugin is enabled. - `--undo` records live in `~/.claude/holyagent/setup-records.json`. - The session-start setup hint checks user, project and local settings, so it stops after a project-scope setup (L39). - `docs/hooks.md` L102-110 covers hooks and the CLI path: - Hooks run `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/holyagent.js`. - The takeover line carries the absolute CLI path, so the CLI path does not depend on scope. - State (`.holyagent/`, state mode in git config, `config.json`) is per clone, not per scope (`docs/usage.md` L89). - I did not verify the plugin data directory. No doc I read mentions `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`. **claude.ai (sourced)** - Chat and Cowork are unified. Plugins are installed from Customize > Plugins and saved to the account. They sync to Claude Code at the next session start ([platform-support](https://claude.com/docs/plugins/platform-support), [support article](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13837440-use-plugins-in-claude)). - Skills load in chat, Cowork and Claude Code. Agents and hooks load in Cowork and Claude Code but are ignored in chat. - A top-level `bin/` makes chat and Cowork refuse the plugin. A plugin `settings` key is ignored in Cowork. - There is no local versus global notion. An install attaches to the account within an organization. An Owner can set a plugin to Not available, Available, Installed by default or Required. - Chat and Cowork load plugins from the account, not from the repo. I found no documented project-level install there. - Current HolyAgent docs are stale. `usage.md` L211 says "does not work there, because of how hooks are activated", contradicting your test. I found no Anthropic source that explains or contradicts that claim, so the doc fix rests on your test alone. - Inference: the plugin's `agent: holyagent` is a `settings` key and is ignored in Cowork. The root would then depend on the session-start hook, as in cloud sessions (`usage.md` L28). **pi (sourced from pi.dev/docs/latest; HolyAgent's docs pin 1.5.0 but I read "latest")** - `pi install` writes to `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`. `-l` writes to `.pi/settings.json`. npm packages land in `~/.pi/agent/npm/` or `.pi/npm/` ([packages](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/packages), [settings](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/settings)). - Project settings override global ones and nested objects merge. Resource lists are combined, and packages in both files load. - Project trust protects `.pi/settings.json`, `.pi/extensions` and project-declared packages ([security](http://pi.dev/docs/latest/security)): - Interactive pi asks once; the answer is saved in `~/.pi/agent/trust.json`. - Print, JSON and RPC modes skip the project's `.pi` resources unless `--approve` or `defaultProjectTrust: "always"` is set. - `defaultProjectTrust` is settable only in the global file. - Declining skips project packages. Context files such as `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` load regardless. - I did not find what happens when the same package is declared at both scopes. - Packages can carry their own `dependencies`. A local-path package is not installed for you (packages doc). **Requirements per install mode** | Host | Global | Project-local | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `claude plugin install --scope user`, then `/holyagent:setup` (sourced) | `--scope project` or `local`, and `setup --scope` to match (sourced) | | claude.ai | Account install; hooks and agents load only in Cowork (sourced) | No equivalent; organization "Required" is the nearest (inference) | | pi | `pi install git:...#holyagent-` (sourced) | `pi install -l`, trust granted, `--approve` for headless specialists (inference) | For pi, the package must bundle its CLI and extension dependencies, or they must be resolvable from the package root. Both scopes install the same way, so resolution should not differ (inference). **Config (inference)** - Per project: `vcs.allowWords`, the `claude` and `pi` sections that choose behavior, and the route table. - Per user: provider login, `defaultProjectTrust`, `npmCommand`. pi already keeps these in `~/.pi/agent`. - `.holyagent/config.json` is per project (`docs/usage.md` L89). A user-level `~/.holyagent/config.json` is not strictly needed for pi. For Claude Code, `setup` already writes to `~/.claude`. **Choices for you** 1. User-level HolyAgent defaults: - (a) None: global installs use the built-in defaults, which is simplest. - (b) Add `~/.holyagent/config.json` merged under the project file. That adds a second schema and merge rules. 2. Which default pi scope to document: - (a) Global first, matching the planned `pi install` command. - (b) Present both equally. - Project-local needs a trust step and does not work headless without `--approve`. 3. Cowork support level: - (a) Support Cowork fully and keep the cloud-style hook takeover. - (b) Document it as partial (chat gets skills only). - The docs need a rewrite either way. **To verify** - The managed-scope precedence rule. - The plugin data directory behavior. - pi behavior when a package is declared at both scopes. - The Cowork hook-activation claim. Compare against the plugin's own docs in your test setup. evidence: Claude scopes: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins (user, project, local); `/home/user/holyagent-docs-t3/docs/usage.md` L95-115 and `docs/hooks.md` L102-110 (what depends on scope) pi scopes: https://pi.dev/docs/latest/packages (`-l`); https://pi.dev/docs/latest/settings (precedence); http://pi.dev/docs/latest/security (trust). The both-scopes duplicate case is not covered by a source. claude.ai: https://claude.com/docs/plugins/platform-support; https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13837440-use-plugins-in-claude; https://claude.com/docs/plugins/org-rollout Choices separated: the "Choices for you" and "To verify" sections above sources: the URLs above, plus `/home/user/holyagent-docs-t3/docs/usage.md`, `docs/pi/installation.md` and `docs/pi/configuration.md`
